extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors in computational mathematics and related fields considering submission to Foundations of Computational Mathematics (FoCM)
extracted.subtask_description: Defines the scope and selection expectations for papers submitted to Foundations of Computational Mathematics (FoCM), emphasizing research at the intersection of mathematics and computation and the requirement for fundamental, innovative advances that deepen understanding of computationally relevant mathematical ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: FoCM publishes outstanding research at the confluence of mathematics and computation. Such research may involve any branch of mathematics — algebra, analysis, geometry, and so forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should lie at the intersection of mathematics and computation; almost any mathematical branch is acceptable provided the work is relevant to computation. This is a topical/subject-matter filter rather than a formatting or length requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hallmark / selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The hallmark of a FoCM paper is that it makes fundamental and innovative advances which further our understanding of deep mathematical ideas underlying modern computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should present fundamental (not merely incremental) and innovative contributions; emphasis is on advancing conceptual understanding of mathematical ideas that underpin computational methods. This is the principal quality criterion for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article type labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles on the site are labeled by type (example shown: 'OriginalPaper').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should choose the appropriate article type (e.g., OriginalPaper) per the journal's submission categories and ensure their manuscript matches the expectations for that category; the page implies distinct article type classifications without listing all types or their specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal Impact Factor 2.7 (2024); 5-year Journal Impact Factor 3.3 (2024); Downloads 238.3k (2025); this journal has 178 open access articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are descriptive metrics of the journal's reach and impact (not acceptance criteria). They may be used by authors/readers to assess the journal's visibility and influence when deciding where to submit or what to cite.
